metadata.Name: POLYGLOT-NER
metadata.Description: A multilingual Named Entity Recognition (NER) dataset for 40 languages, automatically generated using Wikipedia's internal link structure and Freebase attributes. The approach is language-agnostic, relying on word embeddings and techniques like oversampling to handle noise from missing annotations.
metadata.Paper Title: POLYGLOT-NER: Massive Multilingual Named Entity Recognition
metadata.Venue Title: Proceedings of the Seventeenth Conference on Computational Natural Language Learning
metadata.Venue Name: Conference on Computational Natural Language Learning
Affiliations: Department of Computer Science Stony Brook University
metadata.Abstract: The increasing diversity of languages used on the web introduces a new level of complexity to Information Retrieval (IR) systems. We can no longer assume that textual content is written in one language or even the same language family. In this paper, we demonstrate how to build massive multilingual annotators with minimal human expertise and intervention. We describe a system that builds Named Entity Recognition (NER) annotators for 40 major languages using Wikipedia and Freebase. Our approach does not require NER human annotated datasets or language specific resources like treebanks, parallel corpora, and orthographic rules. The novelty of approach lies therein - using only language agnostic techniques, while achieving competitive performance. Our evaluation is two fold: First, we demonstrate the system performance on human annotated datasets. Second, for languages where no gold-standard benchmarks are available, we propose a new method, distant evaluation , based on statistical machine translation.
